newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BRUSSELS BEL-20 INDEX SEEN LOSING 100-200 POINTS.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS BEL-20 INDEX SEEN LOSING 100-200 POINTS.

text.p: The Brussels blue-chip Bel-20 index was pushed into the red on Friday after Wall Street stocks took a tumble and all indicators pointed to a further correction next week.
Dealers said the bourse was at a turning point and expected the Bel-20 to lose between 100 and 200 points in coming weeks.
"The market will come down as quickly as it went up, (the Bel-20) might go down to 1,800, so take your profits, money and run," said one trader.
The Bel-20 closed down 0.70 percent at 2,060.61 points, but fell less than the major European bourses.
The Dow Jones which lost 1.38 percent on Thursday, continued to suffer from profit-taking and stood over one percent lower when the Belgian bourse closed.
Dealers said they had expected a correction following Wall Street's impressive recent bull runs.
"Two weeks ago there were no sellers (in the Belgian market) but now we will have sellers and this will continue in coming days," a trader said.
Retailer Delhaize which was one of the largest gainers at the end of 1996 and early this year suffered the largest losses, down 3.16 percent to 1,990 francs.
Dealers said Delhaize's sharp fall was also in part due to a technical correction after having recently outperformed its U.S. unit Food Lion .
Cement maker CBR was another loser, down 3.08 percent at 3,150 francs.
Despite profit-taking dealers said both Delhaize and CBR remained stocks which would show strong 1997 performances and the stocks would recover once the correction period was over.
Chemical and drugs group UCB was down 1.43 percent at 96,500 due to profit-taking.
